question: Who took charge as the new Chief Minister of Delhi in September 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atishi Marlena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Atishi Marlena** took charge as the Chief Minister of Delhi in **September 2024**, succeeding Arvind Kejriwal.
 
• She is a prominent member of the **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)** and has been a key figure in Delhi's politics.
 
• Atishi has been recognized for her contributions to education reforms in Delhi, including the transformation of government schools.
 
• Her appointment marks a significant milestone, as she is the **first woman Chief Minister of Delhi** from the AAP.
 
• She played a crucial role in the conceptualization and implementation of initiatives like the "Happiness Curriculum" in schools.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi's Administrative Framework**

 
 
• Delhi is a Union Territory with a Legislative Assembly, and its Chief Minister oversees areas such as education, health, and public works.
 
• However, certain powers such as law enforcement fall under the jurisdiction of the Lieutenant Governor.
 
 
 
• **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)**
 
 
• AAP was founded in 2012 by Arvind Kejriwal and others, focusing on anti-corruption and governance reforms.
 
• The party has been in power in Delhi since 2015, with significant focus areas such as education, healthcare, and public welfare.
 
 
 
• **Education Reforms in Delhi**
 
 
• Under AAP’s governance, Delhi saw major overhauls in its education system, including infrastructure improvements and teacher training programs.
 
• Initiatives like the "Happiness Curriculum" and "Entrepreneurship Mindset Curriculum" have garnered international attention.
 
 
 
• **Women in Leadership**
 
 
• Atishi's appointment as Chief Minister adds to the growing number of women in leadership roles in Indian politics.
 
• Her leadership is expected to inspire more women to enter public administration and governance.
